artists.biography:
Mr. Big is an American rock supergroup, formed in Los Angeles, California in 1988. The band is a quartet composed of Eric Martin (lead vocals), Paul Gilbert (guitar), Billy Sheehan (bass guitar), and Pat Torpey (drums); The band is noted especially for their musicianship, and scored a number of hits. Their songs were often marked by strong vocals and vocal harmonies. Their hits include "To Be with You" (a number one single in 15 countries in 1991) and "Green-Tinted Sixties Mind".
Mr. Big have remained active and popular for over two decades, despite internal conflicts and changing music trends. They broke up in 2002, but after requests from fans, they reunited in 2009; their first tour was in Japan, in June 2009. The band released What If..., their first album in 10 years, in January 2011.
The band takes its name from the song by Free, which was eventually covered by the band on their 1993 album, Bump Ahead.

perplexity.description:
Lean into It is the second studio album by American rock supergroup Mr. Big, released on April 2, 1991. The album marked the band's commercial breakthrough, peaking at number 15 on the Billboard 200 and establishing them as significant players in the hard rock landscape of the early 1990s. The record showcased the virtuosic musicianship of the band's lineup, featuring Eric Martin on lead vocals, Paul Gilbert on guitar, and Billy Sheehan on bass, whose technical prowess became a defining characteristic of the album's sound.

The album's most enduring legacy stems from the single "To Be with You," which became Mr. Big's first and only number-one hit on the Billboard Hot 100. The follow-up single "Just Take My Heart" also achieved significant commercial success, reaching number 16 on the same chart. These radio-friendly tracks balanced the album's harder rock elements with accessible melodies, contributing to its broad appeal. The album's cultural footprint extended beyond commercial metrics—it was later ranked number 49 on Rolling Stone's list of the 50 Greatest Hair Metal Albums of All Time, cementing its place within the era's defining genre.

Lean into It exemplified the technical rock and hard rock sound of its era, combining intricate musicianship with radio-accessible songwriting. The album's distinctive cover art, sourced from the historical Montparnasse train accident of 1895, provided a striking visual identity that complemented the music's energy and sophistication.
